title: Verifier context
description: Everything the verifier needs, gathered by a platform adapter. Any CI can produce this file and run `aidd gate --context`.

platform.description: github, gitlab, local, or another adapter name.

trusted.description: False for local runs. An untrusted decision can never be posted as a status.

repo.description: The repository as the adapter names it (`owner/name` on GitHub, the project path on GitLab, the folder name locally). Reports and events show it; no rule reads it.

now.description: The time the gate runs, as an RFC 3339 date-time, such as 2026-09-23T09:00:00Z. The emergency review window is measured from it; when absent, the verifier uses the wall clock, so a conformance case always sets it.

id.description: The PR/MR number or iid, or locally the head ref. Recorded in the gate record; no rule reads it.

url.description: The PR/MR's web address, for links in reports.

author.description: Who opened the change: a platform login, or locally `email:<address>` from git's user.email. An author never approves their own change outside solo.

body.description: The PR/MR description, where the `toml aidd` Change Request block lives (locally, a block naming the Spec the branch adds).

draft.description: True while the PR/MR is a draft; the draft rule keeps the gate pending until it is marked ready.

created_at.description: When the PR/MR was opened (RFC 3339 date-time, such as 2026-09-23T09:00:00Z), or null. Anchors the emergency review window.

change.description: The change under review: a PR/MR, or locally the branch being gated.

head_pushed_at.description: When the head commit reached the platform (RFC 3339 date-time, such as 2026-09-23T09:00:00Z), or null when unknown; the cool-off counts from it, and an unknown time never cools off. Locally, the head commit's committer date.

base_changed_at.description: When the change was last retargeted to another base branch (RFC 3339 date-time, such as 2026-09-23T09:00:00Z), if ever. An approval given before it approved a different diff, so it no longer counts.

path.description: The repo-relative path at head (for a deletion, the path that was deleted).

previous_path.description: For a rename or copy, the path at base; null or absent otherwise. The scope and route rules check it as well as `path`, so a rename cannot move a file out of a protected path unseen.

additions.description: Lines added; counts toward the route's line budget.

deletions.description: Lines deleted; counts toward the route's line budget.

binary.description: True when the diff is binary; a line budget cannot measure it.

files.description: Every file the diff from base_sha to head_sha changes, one entry per path. The route, scope, and budget rules read it.

author.description: The commit author: a platform login, or `email:<address>` when the platform cannot map the email to an account (locally, always the email). Null when unknown.

committer.description: The committer, in the same form as `author`. A committer counts as an author: whoever committed a change cannot approve it. Null when unknown, or when it is the platform itself (list such accounts in `identities.system_accounts`).

message.description: The full commit message, whose `Assisted-by:` and `Co-authored-by:` trailers the provenance rule reads.

merge.description: True for merge commits, which need no provenance trailer.

verified.description: Platform-verified signature. Standard changes require true on every commit.

commits.description: Every commit between base_sha and head_sha. Their authors and committers are the change's authors, who cannot approve it outside solo, and their trailers are the provenance the gate checks.

state.description: The review's verdict. `changes_requested` from anyone whose approval the change needs blocks Merge approval; `commented` never clears an earlier verdict.

commit_sha.description: The commit the review was given on. Null when the platform does not say, and then the review is stale: only an approval that names the head commit counts.

submitted_at.description: When the review was submitted (RFC 3339 date-time, such as 2026-09-23T09:00:00Z), or null. It orders the reviews and starts the approval's cool-off; a null time sorts first and never passes a cool-off or a base change.

verified.description: Local-first only: true when the adapter verified the approval's git signature as good, from a key git trusts (with SSH signing, the approver's own email principal). With platform `local` and `gates.local_approvals = "signed"`, an approval without `verified: true` does not count (`merge_approval.unsigned`). Platforms ignore it.

reviews.description: The platform's reviews on the change, in any order. The verifier sorts them by `submitted_at` and keeps each user's latest that is not `commented`; an `approved` one counts only when it names the head commit. Locally, each `aidd approve merge` recorded on refs/aidd/approvals is an `approved` review.

body.description: The comment text. An approval command counts only on a line of its own, outside quotes, code blocks, and HTML comments.

created_at.description: When the comment was posted (RFC 3339 date-time, such as 2026-09-23T09:00:00Z), or null; it starts the cool-off of an `/aidd approve` line.

edited.description: True when the comment was edited after creation. Approval commands in edited comments never count.

verified.description: Local-first only: true when the adapter verified the approval's git signature, as for reviews. With platform `local` and `gates.local_approvals = "signed"`, an approval line without `verified: true` does not count (`spec_approval.unsigned`, `merge_approval.unsigned`). Platforms ignore it.

comments.description: Comments on the change, where `/aidd approve-spec` (Spec approval) and, under solo, `/aidd approve` lines live. Locally, each approval line recorded on refs/aidd/approvals is a comment.

head_files.description: path -> text for the files the verifier reads, such as the Spec.

base_config.description: Text of .aidd/config.toml at base. Null when the base has none.

extends_texts.description: Pre-fetched parent configs keyed by path or url.

result.description: allow; deny; freeze (only route emergency passes); unbound (no command; fails on the routes in `gates.policy_required_routes`); unreachable (the command did not answer, which counts as deny).

detail.description: The command's own words, shown in the report.

rule.description: The org rule's name; it joins the decision as `policy:<rule>`, and its code is the same.

level.description: The level the Policy command chose for the finding.

message.description: What is wrong, for the report.

fix.description: How to satisfy it, for the report.

findings.description: Org rules the Policy command reported; they join the decision as policy:<rule>.

policy.description: The Policy command's answer, which the adapter runs in a checkout of the base branch. Absent or `unbound` when no command is bound; each finding joins the decision as `policy:<rule>`.

evidence.description: Evidence document, an invalid-artifact record, or null when no run exists for head yet.

commits_truncated.description: True when the platform returned only part of the commit list; authors cannot be verified.

notes.description: What the adapter wants a person to know, such as local approvals that did not count and why. The report shows each note; the decision never reads them.

org_preset.description: Text of an org preset injected by the gate as the implicit root parent of the repo config.

committer_approval_blocked.description: The platform itself stops commit authors from approving (GitLab: prevent approvals by users who add commits), so unlinked commit emails need no finding.

codeowners.description: The base branch's CODEOWNERS text, when the config reads it.

approval_commits.description: For each commit named in a Spec approval line: whether it is an ancestor of head, and the paths it had changed since the base. Proves Spec approval came before implementation.

status_checks.description: State of each named CI check run on head: success, neutral, skipped, failure, cancelled, timed_out, action_required, pending, queued, in_progress, or missing.

sha.description: The merge-group commit the queue built and would move the base branch to. Evidence must be for this commit; `aidd/gate` is posted on it.

ref.description: The queue branch, such as `gh-readonly-queue/main/pr-42-<sha>`. For people; no rule reads it.

base_sha.description: The commit the entry was built on: the base branch tip, or the previous queue entry's commit. Evidence must have run against it.

stacked.description: True when `base_sha` is a previous queue entry rather than the base branch tip, so the entry also carries other pull requests' changes.

tree.description: The tree ID of the merge-group commit.

merged_tree.description: The tree ID the adapter computed by merging the pull request's head (`head_sha`, the commit the approvals bind to) into `base_sha` (`git merge-tree --write-tree`), or null when that merge conflicts.

all_green.description: Whether the platform merges a group only when every entry passed its checks (GitHub: the merge queue rule's `grouping_strategy` is `ALLGREEN`); null when the adapter could not read it.

merge_group.description: Set when the gate judges a merge-queue entry instead of the pull request head. Approvals stay bound to `head_sha`; the tests are re-run on `merge_group.sha`, whose tree must be exactly `head_sha` merged into `merge_group.base_sha`.
